purpose: Casimersen is used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a specific gene mutation that can benefit from skipping exon 45. It is approved for people whose DMD is caused by this particular type of genetic change. It does not cure DMD, but it may help slow the progression of the disease.
how_it_works: Your muscles need a protein called dystrophin to stay strong and work properly. In DMD, a genetic glitch stops your body from making enough of this protein. Casimersen works like a tiny molecular 'patch' that helps your body skip over the broken part of the gene so it can produce a shorter but still somewhat functional version of dystrophin.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like a common cold, cough, fever, joint pain, runny or stuffy nose, headache, pain or discomfort when urinating, and elevated kidney markers in blood tests.
warnings: This medication can affect your kidneys, so your doctor will monitor your kidney function with regular blood and urine tests. Tell your doctor right away if you notice swelling, changes in how much or how often you urinate, or any unusual symptoms. It is given through an IV infusion, so watch for any signs of infusion reactions such as redness, itching, or breathing trouble during or after the infusion.
typical_dosing: Casimersen is given once a week as an intravenous (IV) infusion, meaning it goes directly into your vein. The dose is based on your body weight (30 mg per kilogram of body weight). Each infusion typically takes about 35 to 60 minutes and is given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or infusion center.
